newsitem.title: UK: Pru to sell Italian business to Royal Sun. [CORRECTED 10:03 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Pru to sell Italian business to Royal Sun. [CORRECTED 10:03 GMT]

text.p: Britain's Prudential Corporation said on Thursday it had signed an agreement to sell its Italian life insurance and mutual fund businesses, Prudential Vita SpA, and its two subsidiaries, to Royal SunAlliance Insurance Group Plc for 46 million pounds ($74.6 million).
Prudential said the disposal would have no effect on other operations of the Prudential Group.

Prudential's director responsible for international development, Keith Bedell-Pierce, described the sale as part of a strategic move to sell (corrects from "give away") its relatively small life companies in continental Europe.

"For the moment, our strategic focus remains on the UK, US and the Asia Pacific, but we are undertaking a review of where long-term growth opportunities might arise in continental Europe," Bedell-Pearce said.
The sale follows its move to raise its stake in St James Palace Capital on Wednesday and its successful 2.87 billion pound ($4.7 billion) bid for Scottish Amicable last month.
